description: Patients who have at least one lab record with a recorded RA result other than '-'.

c.request: Looking only at patients without a rheumatoid factor (`RA`) result of '-' in their lab tests, which 10 have the highest average hematocrit (`HCT`) across all their lab records? Show patient `ID`, average uric acid (`UA`) and average hematocrit, highest first, with patients who have no hematocrit values last. Ignore missing values in the averages and don't round. Patients who have at least one lab record with a recorded RA result other than '-'.
c.sql: SELECT ID, AVG(UA) AS average_ua, AVG(HCT) AS average_hematocrit FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN RA = '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0 AND SUM(CASE WHEN RA IS NOT NULL AND RA <> '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 ORDER BY average_hematocrit IS NULL, average_hematocrit DESC, ID LIMIT 10;

a.request: Among patients with at least one laboratory record whose rheumatoid factor (`RA`) result is recorded and is something other than '-', list the 10 with the highest average hematocrit (`HCT`) across all their lab records. Show patient `ID`, average uric acid (`UA`) and average hematocrit, highest hematocrit first, with patients who have no hematocrit values last. Averages ignore missing values. Don't round.
a.sql: SELECT p.ID, AVG(l.UA) AS average_ua, AVG(l.HCT) AS average_hematocrit FROM Patient AS p JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory AS r WHERE r.ID = p.ID AND r.RA IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(r.RA) <> '' AND TRIM(r.RA) <> '-') GROUP BY p.ID ORDER BY average_hematocrit IS NULL, average_hematocrit DESC, p.ID LIMIT 10;

b.request: Among patients with at least one laboratory record where `RA` is recorded and differs from `'-'`, return the 10 patients with the highest average `HCT` across all their laboratory records, showing patient `ID`, average `UA`, and average `HCT`; exclude missing values from each average, leave averages unrounded, sort by average `HCT` descending, and place patients with no `HCT` values last.
b.sql: SELECT p.ID, AVG(l.UA) AS avg_UA, AVG(l.HCT) AS avg_HCT FROM Patient AS p JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory AS ra WHERE ra.ID = p.ID AND ra.RA IS NOT NULL AND ra.RA <> '-') GROUP BY p.ID ORDER BY (AVG(l.HCT) IS NULL), AVG(l.HCT) DESC, p.ID LIMIT 10;
b.raw: Among patients with at least one laboratory record where `RA` is recorded and differs from `'-'`, return the 10 patients with the highest average `HCT` across all their laboratory records, showing patient `ID`, average `UA`, and average `HCT`; exclude missing values from each average, leave averages unrounded, sort by average `HCT` descending, and place patients with no `HCT` values last.

d.request: Among patients with at least one laboratory record where `RA` is recorded and is not '-', return the 10 with the highest average `HCT` across all their laboratory records; show `ID`, average `UA`, and average `HCT`, ignoring null values in each average, without rounding, and placing patients with no `HCT` values last.
d.sql: SELECT l.ID, AVG(l.UA) AS average_UA, AVG(l.HCT) AS average_HCT FROM Laboratory AS l WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory AS r WHERE r.ID = l.ID AND r.RA IS NOT NULL AND r.RA <> '-') GROUP BY l.ID ORDER BY AVG(l.HCT) IS NULL, AVG(l.HCT) DESC, l.ID LIMIT 10;
